newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir says ringgit fall not linked to Petronas.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir says ringgit fall not linked to Petronas.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday that the fall of the ringgit was not linked to threats of sanctions by the United States against state oil firm Petronas.

"It's not the ringgit that went down, it's the dollar that went up, because if you look at the dollar it's been going up against every major currency including the yen," he told reporters after attending a function at power company Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
Mahathir said the fall of the Malaysian currency was probably due to the strength of the dollar ahead of U.S. presidential elections.
"I think it's because of the election that Bill Clinton is going to stand for. It has nothing to do with Petronas," he said. The U.S. elections will take place on Tuesday, Nov 5.
The ringgit fell to a six-month low overnight as U.S. funds and speculators combined rumours and technical reasons to pull down the currency to below 2.53 per dollar.
This compares with the ringgit's Wednesday closing level of 2.5250/60 in Kuala Lumpur, and 2.5135/40 at the close of local Tuesday trading.
Around 0610 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5278/88 a dollar.
